CH and SH

The rule

sh → sh   ·   ch → ch
True most of the time, and the exceptions are the lesson.

Two sounds, no word attached. sh is a long quiet stream of air. ch is a short burst: a t and a sh stuck together.

sh is easy. It is always sh. Every single time, no exceptions, nothing to learn. Everything difficult on this page is ch, which is three sounds wearing one spelling.

chThe ordinary case. chip, chart, chain, charge, switch, chapter, chocolate
kGreek words, and anything where ch meets a consonant. mechanical, technical, technology, chemical, schematic, synchronous, Christmas, chlorine
shFrench words, which kept their French ch. machine, brochure, chef, chassis, parachute, chandelier, champagne, chalet, cliche

Wait, what?

If a consonant follows the ch, it's a k.
Christmas, chrome, chlorine, technical, technology, synchronous.

If a vowel follows, ask where the word came from: Greek gives you k, French gives you sh, and everything else gives you the ordinary ch.

mechanical chemical schematic character echo architecture orchestra chaos

2 · Find the odd one out

Three words. Two of them make the same sound and one does not. Click the one that is different.

3 · Two endings that decide for you

sh
-tion
-cial
-tial
-xual		 All sh, always. The letters look nothing like sh and the sound is sh anyway.
solution connection production commercial potential essential
see Word Stress lesson Same ending you learned to count back from for the stress.
ch
-ture		 Always ch, never t plus you-er.
structure picture future temperature manufacture mixture feature
structure is STRUK-chuh, not struk-TURE.
After a consonant, or with a double s, it is the quiet sh: pressure, session, tension, insure.
Between two vowels, with a single s, it buzzes instead: measure, pleasure, closure, decision, television.
Hand on the throat. Pressure is quiet, measure buzzes.

4 · Say it

Tap either word: the only difference is whether you start with a t.

chair / share
cheat / sheet
cheese / she is
chew / shoe
chips / ships
choose / shoes

ch is just sh with a t stuck on the front. Say sh, then say t-sh.
